housing.summary: London has an expensive, fast-moving rental market. One-bedroom flats in central zones command premium rents; letting agents typically require references, proof of income (often 2.5-3x monthly rent), a right-to-rent immigration check, and a holding deposit. Most tenancies are Assured Shorthold Tenancies (ASTs).

banking.summary: Opening a UK current account usually requires proof of identity and proof of a UK address; newcomers without an address history often use digital banks or basic accounts first. Standard high-street banks offer current accounts once documentation is provided.
required_docs: Proof of UK address (utility bill or tenancy agreement)
Proof of immigration status / visa (BRP or share code)

schools.summary: London offers state (free, catchment/admissions-based), academy, faith, and a large private/independent sector, plus numerous international schools serving expatriate families. State school places are allocated through the local borough council admissions process.

legal_admin.summary: The UK has no universal residents' registration office; local administration is handled by borough councils (e.g. council tax registration). Immigration status is managed centrally through UK Visas and Immigration, and newcomers register with local services (council, GP) after arrival.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register for council tax with your London borough council and confirm your immigration status/visa with the Home Office; obtain a National Insurance number for work.

tax_finance.summary: Income tax and National Insurance are administered by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC). Employees are typically taxed at source via PAYE; new arrivals need a National Insurance number to work and may need to register with HMRC.

transport.summary: London's integrated public transport network is run by Transport for London (TfL), covering the Underground, Overground, Elizabeth line, buses, DLR, trams and river services. Fares use a zonal system with contactless/Oyster pay-as-you-go capping; monthly Travelcards are available by zone range.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA and certain designated-country licences can be exchanged or used for a period; others may need to pass a UK driving test. Check DVLA rules for your issuing country.
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with a local GP (general practitioner) surgery to access NHS primary care; most visa holders pay the Immigration Health Surcharge for NHS access.
